coordinates.locator: OSM way 51755116 "CDF Hall" building centroid (extract of 2026-09-18)
coordinates.note: The CDF collision hall (B0) footprint is mapped in OpenStreetMap as the named building 'CDF Hall'; the coordinate is its centroid, within about 40 m of the hall. It is shown as approximate because OpenStreetMap is a community map and not a survey; the 40 m precision is the half-size of the footprint. It replaces a Fermilab campus point of 3 km precision.

name: CDF collision hall (Tevatron B0)
notes: The point is the centroid of the 'CDF Hall' building as mapped in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note). No survey or official source consulted gives a dedicated lat/lon for this interaction hall.

The INSPIRE experiment record long_name for CDF is "Study of Proton Anti-proton Collisions Using a Large Detector at B0 -- the CDF Detector" (src:colliders-historical-cdf-inspire-experiment-record), confirming the B0 location name, though not coordinates.

summary.plain: The interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring where the CDF detector sat, in Batavia, Illinois. Its position is the centroid of the hall building as traced in OpenStreetMap, not a surveyed point.
summary.technical: CDF collision hall (Tevatron B0): one of the Tevatron ring's interaction regions, at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. No dedicated survey coordinate for the hall itself was found; shown at Fermilab campus precision (~3 km) as an approximate marker.
